questions.question: What is the expected major product when Racemic (±)-lactic acid is treated with (R)-1-Phenylethylamine?
questions.explanation: Treating Racemic (±)-lactic acid with (R)-1-Phenylethylamine yields Diastereomeric salt pair (separable by crystallization). Rationale: Reacting an enantiomeric pair with a single chiral amine yields diastereomeric salts with different solubilities.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of (S)-2-Bromobutane into 2,2-Dibromobutane (achiral) + 2,3-Dibromobutane (diastereomers)?
questions.explanation: To convert (S)-2-Bromobutane into 2,2-Dibromobutane (achiral) + 2,3-Dibromobutane (diastereomers), the appropriate reagent is Br2 / hν. Rationale: Abstraction at C2 destroys the stereocenter via a planar radical intermediate; abstraction at C3 creates a second stereocenter.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when (R)-2-Bromooctane is treated with Sodium iodide (NaI) in acetone?
questions.explanation: Treating (R)-2-Bromooctane with Sodium iodide (NaI) in acetone yields (S)-2-Iodooctane + NaBr. Rationale: Backside nucleophilic attack by iodide inverts the tetrahedral chiral center completely (Walden inversion).

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Propanoic acid into Racemic (±)-2-bromopropanoic acid?
questions.explanation: To convert Propanoic acid into Racemic (±)-2-bromopropanoic acid, the appropriate reagent is 1. Br2, PBr3; 2. H2O. Rationale: Attack at the planar enol intermediate occurs with equal probability from top (re) and bottom (si) faces.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Equimolar mixture of (R)- and (S)-carvone is treated with Polarimeter (589 nm)?
questions.explanation: Treating Equimolar mixture of (R)- and (S)-carvone with Polarimeter (589 nm) yields Zero net optical rotation ([α] = 0°). Rationale: A 50:50 racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation because equal and opposite rotations cancel.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of cis-2-Butene into (2R,3R)- and (2S,3S)-Dibromobutane (racemic pair)?
questions.explanation: To convert cis-2-Butene into (2R,3R)- and (2S,3S)-Dibromobutane (racemic pair), the appropriate reagent is Br2 in CH2Cl2. Rationale: Anti-addition of bromonium ion to cis-alkene produces a pair of chiral enantiomers.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Br2 in CH2Cl2 to yield meso-2,3-Dibromobutane as the major product?
questions.explanation: trans-2-Butene reacts with Br2 in CH2Cl2 to yield meso-2,3-Dibromobutane. Rationale: Anti-addition across the trans-double bond yields the achiral meso diastereomer with an internal mirror plane.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Pyruvate is treated with NADH / Lactate dehydrogenase?
questions.explanation: Treating Pyruvate with NADH / Lactate dehydrogenase yields (S)-Lactate (pure enantiomer). Rationale: The chiral active site of the enzyme directs hydride transfer exclusively to the re-face of pyruvate.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with mCPBA to yield trans- and cis-Epoxy-4-methylcyclohexane (diastereomeric mixture) as the major product?
questions.explanation: (R)-4-Methylcyclohexene reacts with mCPBA to yield trans- and cis-Epoxy-4-methylcyclohexane (diastereomeric mixture). Rationale: The pre-existing chiral center creates diastereotopic faces with unequal steric accessibility.

questions.topic: Tosylation with retention followed by SN2
questions.question: What is the expected major product when (R)-2-Butanol is treated with 1. TsCl, pyridine; 2. NaCN?
questions.explanation: Treating (R)-2-Butanol with 1. TsCl, pyridine; 2. NaCN yields (S)-2-Methylbutanenitrile. Rationale: Tosylation breaks the O-H bond (retention); subsequent SN2 displacement of tosylate by cyanide inverts configuration.
